title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k algebraically closed, X^n smooth connected projective, Y^{n-1} a smooth hyperplane section. Three adequate equivalence relations on codimension-i cycles: A^i_r (rational, i.e. Chow groups CH^i), A^i_a (algebraic) and A^i_τ (τ-equivalence, i.e. numerical/homological modulo torsion, as in SGA6 for divisors). Grothendieck writes 'Lefschetz-type' conjectures for Chow groups, modelled on the cohomological weak Lefschetz theorem: H^k(X) -> H^k(Y) is an isomorphism for k < n-1 and injective for k = n-1. A crossed-out table at the top summarises the pattern bijective / injective / bijective-on-τ-part with an 'exc. p' (exceptional p-torsion in characteristic p) caveat.

(1) Restriction CH^i(X) -> CH^i(Y).
- 2i <= n-2: bijective, perhaps away from p. This is the higher-codimension analogue of the Grothendieck–Lefschetz theorem for Pic in SGA2 (i=1, dim Y >= 3).
- 2i = n-1: injective, and bijective on the τ-trivial subgroups CH^i(-)^τ. He deduces that the algebraically trivial parts correspond bijectively and that A^i_τ(X) -> A^i_τ(Y) is injective. For n=3, i=1 this is Pic^0 X ≅ Pic^0 Y together with NS(X)/tors -> NS(Y)/tors injective, the Noether–Lefschetz pattern.
- 2i = n: injective on τ-trivial subgroups. For n=2 this is Pic^τ X -> Pic^τ Y.

(2) Gysin pushforward CH_i(Y) -> CH_i(X) (i = dimension).
- 2i <= n-3: bijective (p?).
- 2i = n-2: surjective, surjective on τ-parts, bijective on algebraic-equivalence groups.

The next page continues with (3), a hard-Lefschetz analogue for cycles modulo algebraic or rational equivalence, deriving injectivity or surjectivity of E^p modulo finite groups.

Purpose: an attempt to formulate, beside the standard conjectures, a motivic/Chow-level Lefschetz theory. Today such statements are expected as consequences of the Bloch–Beilinson–Murre filtration plus the standard conjectures.
errors: (2) as written is false for rational equivalence. Take n=3, i=0 (2i=0<=n-3): X=P^3, Y a smooth quartic K3 surface. CH_0(Y)->CH_0(P^3)=Z is not injective, since CH_0(Y)_hom is huge (Mumford). Under Bloch–Beilinson, gr^j CH_i(Y) is governed by H_{2i+j}(Y) for j up to the codimension n-1-i. The Gysin map on homology is an isomorphism only for degree <= n-2, so the pushforward on Chow groups cannot be bijective (only surjectivity-type statements are plausible). Weak Lefschetz for Chow groups is not self-dual the way cohomology is.

In (1), case 2i=n-1, read literally with A^i_a = cycles modulo algebraic equivalence, 'A^i_a(X)->A^i_a(Y) bijective' would contradict Noether–Lefschetz (e.g. a quartic surface in P^3 containing a line has NS of rank >1). It is also inconsistent with the next line, where the τ-quotients are only injective. It must mean the subgroups of algebraically trivial cycles. With that reading it is consistent.

On the next page, (3), hard Lefschetz bijectivity 'mod finite groups' for cycles modulo algebraic equivalence fails because of Griffiths groups. For a general quintic threefold, A^2_a has infinite-rank Griffiths group (Clemens), while NS is finitely generated.

ideas.what: Weak Lefschetz for Chow groups: restriction CH^i(X)->CH^i(Y) bijective for 2i<=n-2, injective (bijective on homologically trivial parts) for 2i=n-1, with possible p-torsion exceptions
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz conjecture for Chow groups / Hartshorne's question; consequence of Bloch–Beilinson–Murre conjectures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hartshorne (1975, Equivalence relations on algebraic cycles and subvarieties of small codimension); later Paranjape (1994), Bloch–Beilinson framework
ideas.where_published: Only the i=1 case (Grothendieck–Lefschetz for Pic) appears in SGA2

ideas.what: Dual statement for Gysin pushforward on cycles of small dimension
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz for Chow groups of small-dimensional cycles (e.g. CH_0 of ample divisors)

ideas.what: Tracking the three equivalences (rational, algebraic, τ) separately with 'exc. p' torsion caveats
ideas.modern_name: filtration CH ⊃ CH_hom ⊃ CH_alg and Lefschetz behaviour on each graded piece

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulated Chow-group-level weak Lefschetz conjectures for arbitrary smooth projective X and smooth hyperplane sections, distinguishing rational/algebraic/τ equivalence. This predates Hartshorne's published question (restricted to hypersurfaces/complete intersections) and the Bloch–Beilinson framework that explains it.
missed.quote: A^i_r(X) -> A^i_r(Y) ... 2i <= n-2 ... bijectif [exc. p ?] ... 2i = n-1 ... injectif [exc. p] induit A^i_r(X)^τ -> A^i_r(Y)^τ bijectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority note. The general form, including the middle cases, matches what Bloch–Beilinson predicts. The dual pushforward version on this page is false (Mumford), showing the asymmetry was not yet understood.

deep.surprise_reason: These are unpublished Chow-level Lefschetz conjectures by Grothendieck, likely c. 1965–71, anticipating Hartshorne's 1975 question and Bloch–Beilinson consequences. They are not mathematically new today, and part (2) is false.
transcription_corrections: In the implication under 2i=n-1, 'A^i_a(X)->A^i_a(Y) bijectif' should almost certainly be read as the subgroups of algebraically trivial classes, not the quotient groups.
In (2) the bound is '2i <= n-3, i.e. i <= (n-3)/2 = (n-1)/2 - 1' (struck intermediate computation).
